PullRequest.Title: extensions: restore installed MCP and plugin sections
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary - restore installed-only MCP Servers and Agent Plugins sections in the Extensions view - keep the Extensions filters on `@mcp` and `@agentPlugins`, including when customization marketplace discovery is enabled - route **MCP: Browse MCP Servers** to Customizations Discover with the MCP filter in both the workbench and Agents window - simplify the marketplace redirect empty states by removing decorative icons and using the standard heading/body font ramp - abbreviate marketplace star counts using the Extensions list convention while retaining exact accessible labels Closes #341074 ## Validation - `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/customizationMarketplaceWelcome.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/browser/mcpServersView.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentPluginsView.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/browser/mcpCommands.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/browser/mcp.contribution.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/test/browser/mcpCommands.test.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentPluginsView.test.ts` — passed - `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed - `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationDiscoveryPage.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationDiscoveryPage.test.ts` — passed - `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\aiCustomization\aiCustomizationDiscoveryPage.test.ts --grep "search results render compact star counts"` — 1 test passed - `.\scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/test/browser/mcpCommands.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentPluginsView.test.ts` — 6 tests passed - `npm run typecheck-client` — passed - manually verified the restored installed Agent Plugins section - manually verified `@mcp` and `@agentPlugins` redirect empty states with `chat.customizations.marketplace.enabled: true` - manually verified the MCP Servers and Agent Plugins Extensions filters populate `@mcp ` and `@agentPlugins ` respectively - manually verified **MCP: Browse MCP Servers** opens Discover with `@type:mcp` in both the workbench and Agents window ## Screenshots ### Marketplace redirects | Before | After | | --- | --- | | MCP Servers

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added descriptor, empty-query path, awaited view loading, and IPC fan-out are directly traced. The exact delay depends on local versus remote topology and server count, but the redundant boundary calls and full-list serialization are deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: shared-process and remote-agent IPC calls plus serialization of installed MCP server records
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each activation of the default Extensions views or return to an empty search performs one grouped installed-server refresh; the two IPC reads run in parallel, and bytes/object mapping scale with the total installed MCP servers across local and remote scopes.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased Extensions-view latency and unnecessary IPC/serialization work
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Opening the default Extensions view did not create an MCP list and therefore issued no MCP management getInstalled request; McpWorkbenchService had already populated and maintained its local server cache eagerly through its constructor and install/update/uninstall/profile events.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added default installed-MCP descriptor creates McpServersListView with an empty query. ExtensionsViewlet calls show('') for each visible default view, which reaches queryLocal(); that unconditionally calls IWorkbenchMcpManagementService.getInstalled again before the new section can finish loading.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 488 newly instantiates McpServersListView as a default installed section; with the default empty query this descriptor adds the redundant queryLocal/IPC path to every Extensions default-view activation.
Findings.Title: Render installed MCP servers from the populated cache
Findings.Impact: For users with installed MCP servers, opening Extensions or clearing a search now adds shared-process IPC and, in remote workspaces, a remote-agent IPC round trip to the view-loading Promise.all. This serializes/maps the full installed-server list even though `mcpWorkbenchService.local` already contains the authoritative event-maintained snapshot, delaying section readiness and adding work on every reactivation.
Findings.Evidence: ExtensionsViewlet.showExtensionsViews awaits every visible AbstractExtensionsListView.show call. The new descriptor is visible under DefaultViewsContext; McpServersListView.show('') calls query(''), whose local branch awaits mcpWorkbenchService.queryLocal(). McpWorkbenchService.queryLocal calls mcpManagementService.getInstalled; WorkbenchMcpManagementService fans that into shared/local, remote, and workspace reads, and McpManagementChannelClient.getInstalled is an IPC channel.call that serializes the returned array. McpWorkbenchService already starts queryLocal in its eager constructor and maintains `_local` from management events.
Findings.Recommendation: Give the installed descriptor a cached-local mode: await `whenInitialLocalMcpServersLoaded`, build the model from `mcpWorkbenchService.local`, and retain the existing onChange/onReset listeners. Reserve queryLocal/getInstalled for explicit cache refresh or profile changes already handled by the service.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The DI activation, AfterRestored timing, and discovery filesystem/watcher call path are explicit. Normal MCP-enabled sessions may already instantiate the service, but the reported MCP-disabled/no-plugin-use trigger deterministically changes from no discovery to eager discovery; only exact wall-clock magnitude varies by plugin count and filesystem.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem resolves, file reads, directory watchers, and per-plugin component objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: On every workbench restore, cost grows with configured, marketplace-installed, Copilot CLI, and extension-contributed plugins; each discovered plugin resolves its root and manifest and initializes observers/watchers for commands, skills, agents, rules, automations, hooks, and MCP definitions.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: unnecessary post-restore I/O, CPU/GC pressure, and contention with initial user interaction
Findings.PreviousBehavior: AgentPluginsViewsContribution only registered actions and view descriptors, so IAgentPluginService remained delayed unless MCP discovery or an actual chat/plugin consumer requested it. In sessions with MCP access disabled and no plugin use, startup performed none of this plugin discovery.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added constructor dependency resolves the delayed IAgentPluginService as soon as the AfterRestored contribution is created, and AgentPluginService immediately constructs and starts all four discovery providers before the Extensions container or installed-plugin section is requested.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The newly added `@IAgentPluginService agentPluginService` constructor parameter at RIGHT line 687 forces resolution of a previously delayed heavyweight service during the always-created AfterRestored view-registration contribution.
Findings.Title: Defer plugin discovery until the installed view is needed
Findings.Impact: With MCP access set to none (a realistic managed configuration) and no chat/plugin interaction, every startup now probes the Copilot CLI config, resolves all configured/installed plugin roots and manifests, and retains their filesystem watchers solely to compute a context key for a view the user may never open. Large plugin sets amplify the post-startup I/O and allocation and can make the restored workbench less responsive.
Findings.Evidence: chat.view.contribution.ts registers this contribution at WorkbenchPhase.AfterRestored; chat.shared.contribution.ts registers IAgentPluginService as InstantiationType.Delayed. AgentPluginService's constructor creates every registered discovery and calls start(); those starts schedule _refreshPlugins, and _discoverAndBuildPlugins performs fileService.resolve/detectPluginFormat/readPluginManifest and creates per-component/root watchers. McpDiscovery does not instantiate PluginMcpDiscovery when mcpAccess is None, establishing a pre-diff configuration where this service could remain dormant.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep view registration lightweight and resolve/observe IAgentPluginService only when the Extensions container/default installed-plugin view is first activated (retaining the observer afterward), or expose a genuinely lightweight installed-presence signal that does not start full plugin discovery.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench restore with agent plugins unused, especially when MCP access is disabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: AgentPluginsViewsContribution is created at AfterRestored, so the work does not block the restore barrier but immediately competes with post-restore interaction. The new constructor dependency synchronously creates the service/discovery graph; scheduled filesystem discovery then runs asynchronously.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve configured/installed plugin roots, probe plugin format, read manifests and Copilot CLI config, enumerate component directories, and create file watchers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One refresh per each of four discovery providers at activation; root/manifest work scales with effective unique plugin URIs, followed by component path reads/watchers per plugin.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The delayed service was not requested by AgentPluginsViewsContribution; with MCP access None and no chat/plugin use, these boundaries were absent until actual feature use.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the restore barrier but on the immediate post-restore resource path, where it can contend for filesystem, CPU, and GC with first interaction.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Four discovery providers and the effective union of configured, marketplace-installed, Copilot CLI, and extension-contributed plugin roots; per discovered plugin, manifest/component paths and retained watchers scale with plugin count and components.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The four providers schedule refreshes independently. Each provider walks its source list sequentially, while each built plugin initializes multiple component observables/promises and watchers. There is no startup gate tied to Extensions-view visibility.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: IAgentPluginService is a session singleton, so discovery is not reconstructed repeatedly in one session. OS/file-service caches may make warm reads cheaper, but the service still probes sources and creates retained watchers. Before the diff it could remain wholly uninstantiated in MCP-disabled sessions with no plugin consumer.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: DI timing, delayed registration, discovery startup, and filesystem/watcher operations are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Normal MCP-enabled sessions often already activate PluginMcpDiscovery, reducing incremental work there. The regression is deterministic for MCP-disabled/no-plugin-use sessions, while duration varies with filesystem and plugin count.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable eager-work regression; the installed-view context key activates full plugin discovery before the view is requested.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Extensions container in its default state with installed MCP servers and/or agent plugins
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ExtensionsViewlet.showExtensionsViews awaits all visible list views in a Promise.all. The new MCP installed view's empty query awaits queryLocal/getInstalled before its model is ready. The agent-plugin installed view maps the already discovered plugin cache synchronously.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch installed MCP servers through shared-process and, for remote workspaces, remote-agent McpManagementChannelClient.getInstalled calls, then deserialize/map the returned arrays.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One grouped refresh per default Extensions-view activation; up to two IPC calls in parallel plus the workspace source, serializing all installed records once per source.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No default MCP section existed, so opening Extensions did not issue this MCP management refresh; the eager workbench service cache was populated independently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by the new section and the Extensions view's aggregate progress Promise, delaying section readiness.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total installed MCP records across user, remote-user, and workspace scopes; agent-plugin rendering scales with cached installed plugin count and virtualized visible rows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Visible Extensions sections load concurrently. A single MCP queryLocal fans out with Promise.all to shared/local, remote, and workspace management sources; it is grouped rather than per server, but repeated on each default-view reactivation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: McpWorkbenchService eagerly populates `_local` and maintains it from install/update/uninstall/profile events, but the new view bypasses that warm cache and invokes getInstalled again. Underlying management services may have initialized data, yet shared-process and remote IPC plus full-list serialization still occur. Agent-plugin installed querying uses cached marketplace/plugin observables and adds no view-time I/O.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the descriptor, empty-query branch, management fan-out, and IPC implementation are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Installed MCP sets are usually small, but remote round-trip duration varies. The redundant IPC mechanism and O(server-count) serialization are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated boundary work; use the existing authoritative local cache for this installed-only section.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run MCP Browse, Extensions MCP/Agent Plugins browse actions, or Show Installed MCP Servers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: MCP Browse awaits opening the Customizations editor, after which visible discovery results wait on a marketplace query. Extensions browse actions await opening/searching the Extensions container; with customization marketplace enabled, the MCP/plugin redirect welcome returns an empty model without marketplace fetch. Show Installed first opens the default Extensions state and then focuses the installed MCP view.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query the customization marketplace when the MCP discovery page becomes visible.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one 100-item browse request; pagination is user-driven, while mixed-type filtered backfill is capped at eight sequential pages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The MCP Browse command previously opened Extensions with @mcp, using the MCP gallery/redirect path rather than this customization marketplace path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Results wait for the request, but editor opening itself completes first.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query Extensions recommendations/default gallery views when Show Installed resets the Extensions search to empty.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the normal default-view grouped gallery queries, subject to existing gallery/cache/configuration behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The command previously opened the customization management editor rather than resetting the Extensions container.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These default sections load asynchronously alongside the target view; they are not awaited by the subsequent openView call as an explicit network dependency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One navigation action; catalog pages are 100 items for browse and 24 for search, with up to eight pages only for mixed-type backfill. Installed navigation scales with visible default sections and installed MCP records.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Catalog pages are sequential and cancellable; source fan-out is encapsulated by the marketplace service. Extensions default sections load concurrently. Show Installed does not launch per-server requests.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The discovery page caches the empty-query browse page by source for its lifetime and cancels replaced requests. Plugin marketplace fetches use service snapshots/coalescing; redirect welcome mode performs no fetch. The installed MCP cache bypass is covered by the submitted finding.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for routing and bounded request behavior; lower user-visible impact because marketplace loading is asynchronous and action-driven.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Network source count, caches, and whether recommendation views are enabled vary. The routing is intentional and request counts remain bounded, so no separate high-confidence regression beyond the reported installed-MCP refresh.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: routing changes are bounded and user-triggered; the concrete cache-bypass cost is already reported.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render Customizations discovery rows and marketplace redirect welcome content
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Formatting runs only while a virtualized result row is rendered. Welcome construction renders a small fixed heading, markdown description, and button when its view body is created.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible virtualized rows (page size 24 for search) and a fixed number of welcome DOM nodes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI rendering on the list render path; no added async work or boundary concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: List virtualization reuses templates; compact count formatting has no cache but constant cost. Removing the welcome icon reduces DOM nodes. No cache semantics changed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact render time is unmeasured, but changed operations are constant-time and reduce or preserve work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression: compact numeric formatting is O(1), accessible locale formatting already existed, and the welcome change removes DOM/style work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 10 changed files and all diff pages. Submitted two findings: eager activation of full agent-plugin discovery at AfterRestored, and redundant installed-MCP IPC refreshes from the new default Extensions section. Command routing, virtualized star formatting, welcome DOM/CSS, and tests add no further reportable performance regression.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
